content: I have recently put a massive amount of work into breaking the defeq of docs#MonoidAlgebra and docs#AddMonoidAlgebra with docs#Finsupp, see #38714. This is only a small part of my greater ambition of unifying the MonoidAlgebra-like definitions on one hand, unifying Finsupp and DFinsupp on the other hand, and breaking the defeqs between the two worlds. I would like to relocate all the various discussions regarding this to the current thread.

Here is the current plan:

  1. Make PowerSeries/MvPowerSeries (abbrevs over the same) one-field structure.
  2. Redefine Polynomial R as an abbrev of AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ. Note that MvPolynomial already is an abbrev for the relevant AddMonoidAlgebra.

  3. Unify the APIs for the MonoidAlgebra-like types, in particular

    • Name the conversion functions to and from Finsupp ofCoeff and coeff respectively.
    • Come up with a consistent folder structure. I suggest one folder per MonoidAlgebra-like type, with one file for the boilerplate instances and definitions transferred from Finsupp, one file for the convolution multiplication, further files for type-specific constructions.
    • I don't have a strong opinion where the folders themselves should live. @Filippo A. E. Nuccio suggested RingTheory. Currently they are split half-half between RingTheory and Algebra.

  4. Sort out what the "families" of types there are out there. Currently, I believe there are the following ones:

    • Finsupp is a special-case of DFinsupp.
    • Polynomial and MvPolynomial are special-cases of AddMonoidAlgebra. SkewPolynomial is a special of SkewAddMonoidAlgebra (currently missing). MonoidAlgebra is a special-case of SkewMonoidAlgebra (not syntactically unfortunately, because the latter assumes an action of the monoid on the ring, and the former is what you get if that action is trivial). Both are a (syntactic) special-case of CrossProductAlgebra (from BrauerGroup).
    • PowerSeries and MvPowerSeries are (syntactic) special cases of LargeMonoidAlgebra (currently unimplemented, see #maths > Hahn Series for mathematical discussion).
    • LaurentSeries is a special-case of HahnSeries.

  5. In each family, make each special-case an abbrev of the most general type. This might have performance impact but it is expected to reduce code duplication hugely. For example, most of the Algebra.Polynomial folder could be simply gone.
if you can keep the computable property of DFinsupp it would be really appreciated, because lean-units rely on it.
Looking forward for this as well, I'll be learning a lot from it :)

Alfredo Moreira-Rosa said:

if you can keep the computable property of DFinsupp it would be really appreciated

The plan is the opposite, Finsupp would become computable
#new members > Finsupp noncomputability
#mathlib4 > Computable/decidable Finsupp?
Snir is both correct and wrong in the sense that this is the plan, but that it isn't opposite to keeping DFinsupp computable :-)

I will now advertise the PRs that are working towards the goals stated at the start of the thread. I am requesting @Eric Wieser's review on each of them because he is interested in seeing them, but he told me that the PRs should not be blocked waiting on him!
• #41365 chore(Algebra/SkewPolynomial): rename the conversion functions to coeff/ofCoeff

Yaël Dillies said:

Redefine Polynomial R as an abbrev of AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ. Note that MvPolynomial already is an abbrev for the relevant AddMonoidAlgebra.

Is it clear that this is a good idea? I seem to recall this was controversial some time ago, but maybe I'm misremembering. In either case, what's the motivation for this change (and not making MvPolynomial a def)?
I think the main argument against it some time ago was that we really didn't want Polynomial to be defeq to Finsupp

We fixed that originally by adding a barrier between Polynomial and AddMonoidAlgebra, but it has retrostpectively been mine and Yael's position that this barrier is needed but in the wrong place. #38714 added one in the right place, which lets us explore removing the one in the wrong place

The other point is that polynomial rings are mathematically special cases of monoid algebras, and there is no instance on one that we wouldn't want on the other. This is compared to monoid algebras which can be represented as finitely supported functions, but on which we want different operations (multiplication, among others).

I opened a draft PR #41472 on large monoid algebra(temporarily named it TotalMonoidAlgebra to align with the wiki page total algebra and is open to other names). It adapts constructions in MonoidAlgebra/Defs.lean to large monoid case (e.g. replacing M →₀ R to M → R, removing induction principles, using [Finset.HasAntidiagonal M] to define convolution products and so on)
Also pinging @María Inés de Frutos Fernández who has been recently working on Skew Polynomials.

I think that @Yaël Dillies 's plan is excellent, I've recently been playing with MvPolynomials (their degrees, in particular) and there are a lot of defeq abused largely caused by things being defs. Concerning RingTheory vs Algebra, I'm not sure I was suggesting anything, mostly observing that results about (Mv)polynomials should not be split in two places. What I would probably suggest is that

  • (Add)MonoidAlgebra
  • SkewMonoidAlgebra
  • CrossProductAlgebra
    stay in Algebra and that everything concerning Polynomial, MvPolynomial, PowerSeries and LaurentSeries land in RingTheory. I'm less decided about HahnSeries, but I would probably let them be in Algebra.
